# Capture a cheap-mode dispatched audit to measure Phase 2 PARALLELISM benefit

discovered-from:WL-0MUFD33FT0080OD5

## Finding

The mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` code is live in the running `dev` build
(herdr `dist/` rebuilt 2026-09-24 18:38 and contains the WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME wiring;
the running checkout HEAD `e1bea036` includes `6188a90d`). A `dev`→`main` release is
**not** required for the change to take effect.

The first full post-change cheap window (2026-09-25 01:00-10:00) contained **no
dispatched audits** — the downtime dispatcher selected only implement/plan/intake/
scheduled items (last audit dispatch was 2026-09-24T23:54Z in fast mode; no
`audit-*` pi sessions started in the window). Because the `PARALLELISM=2` path is
audit-only, it was never exercised, so the Phase 2 benefit is unmeasured.

Window-level metrics (proxy host 192.168.0.199): remote fallback 41.7% post vs 52.8%
pre; cheap busy 67.7% both; **avg concurrency while busy 1.72 post vs 1.46 pre**;
total compute 9h 39m post vs 7h 43m pre (both confounded by differing workload).

## Goal

As the operator, I want at least one dispatched audit to run during a cheap window so I
can measure whether mode-aware `PARALLELISM=2` makes its Phase 2 children overlap the
parent and shortens Phase 2 wall-clock, without raising remote fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. At least one dispatched audit runs in a 01:00-10:00 cheap window, and
   `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` is confirmed on the audit pane (e.g. via
   `/proc/<pid>/environ`).
2. **Primary (per-audit A/B):** the cheap-mode `PARALLELISM=2` audit's Phase 2 wall-clock
   and child overlap (peak concurrency 2 during Phase 2) are compared against a
   `PARALLELISM=1` audit — matched item, or alternating — and reported.
3. **Secondary (window guardrails):** cheap-window **avg concurrency (while busy)** and
   **slot utilisation (total compute ÷ window × slots)** are compared against the
   immediate pre-change cheap windows (2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24, 01:00-10:00),
   normalised for audit/request volume, and reported.
4. Remote fallback rate does not increase vs the pre-change comparison.
5. Findings recorded on WL-0MUFD33FT0080OD5.

## Proposed remedy (pick one)

- Prefer audit-tier work items for downtime dispatch during cheap windows, so the new
  path is exercised; or
- Trigger one manual cheap-window audit and capture the spawn env plus the proxy report;
  or
- Extend the observation period until a dispatched audit lands in cheap mode.

## Notes

- **Do not use busy % as the success metric** — it saturates at one active slot and is
  blind to the second cheap slot the change is meant to use. Use avg concurrency /
  slot utilisation plus per-audit Phase 2 wall-clock. Busy % and fallback are guardrails.
- Reference-only baseline: `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-08-22_3/` (04:00-05:00 38.2%,
  05:00-06:00 24.8% busy; cheap avg concurrency 1.55, peak 4). Same-day variance of the
  2026-08-22 runs was large, so window metrics alone are weak evidence.
- Proxy logs/reports live on 192.168.0.199 (`/var/log/llama-proxy`,
  `~/proxy-usage-reports`), reachable over SSH. Use an isolated `--output-dir` when
  re-running the report.
data.title: Capture a cheap-mode dispatched audit to measure Phase 2 PARALLELISM benefit

# Align Herdr STAGES/STAGE_MAP/StageFilter with the CLI vocabulary

## Goal

As a Herdr user, I want the stage filter to cycle only through stages the `wl`
CLI recognises (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`, `done`),
so I never land on a filter that can only ever be empty.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `STAGES` equals exactly the CLI stage vocabulary `['idea','intake_complete','plan_complete','in_review','done']`; `in_progress` and `completed` are removed.
- [ ] `Stage` (and any derived types) continue to typecheck, and no Herdr code hard-codes the removed `in_progress`/`completed` values as valid stages.
- [ ] `STAGE_MAP` accepts only CLI-valid canonical names and supported shorthand aliases; the `progress → in_progress` alias is removed while `intake`/`plan`/`review`/`done` aliases still resolve, and any `completed` mapping is removed.
- [ ] `StageFilter` cycles only the five valid stages (then clears to `null`).
- [ ] `/wl progress` and `/wl completed` fail soft (no crash, no invalid filter applied), consistent with the existing `/wl <bogus>` behaviour.
- [ ] Tests are added/updated for the exact `STAGES` list, `StageFilter` cycling/wrapping and `STAGE_MAP` alias resolution plus invalid-alias fail-soft.

## Minimal Implementation

- Trim `STAGES` to the five CLI stages; update the `Stage` union and any consumers.
- Trim `STAGE_MAP`: delete the `progress`/`in_progress` entries and any `completed` mapping.
- Update the `/wl <stage>` help/option lists to the aligned vocabulary.
- Add/adjust unit tests in `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
- `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: none.

## Deliverables

- Aligned `STAGES`, `Stage` type, `STAGE_MAP` and `StageFilter`.
data.title: Align Herdr STAGES/STAGE_MAP/StageFilter with the CLI vocabulary

# Guard fetchItemsByStage against invalid stages

## Goal

As a Herdr user, I want an invalid stage filter to fail soft rather than issue
a `wl list --stage <invalid>` call and show a misleading empty worklist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` `fetchItemsByStage` guards unknown/invalid stages fail-soft: it never issues `wl list --stage <invalid>` and never throws (returns an empty or fallback list).
- [ ] `STAGE_STATUS` no longer supplies a status mapping for the removed stages `in_progress`/`completed`.
- [ ] A regression test proves `in_progress`/`completed`/`bogus` cannot produce a CLI invocation and do not throw.
- [ ] Valid stages (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`, `done`) keep their existing status behaviour.
- [ ] `tests/herdr/fetcher.test.ts` no longer asserts that `fetchItemsByStage('in_progress')`/`('completed')` returns items.

## Minimal Implementation

- Validate the requested stage against the canonical `STAGES` list before calling `runWl`.
- Return an empty list for invalid stages without spawning the CLI.
- Update the fetcher regression tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
- `tests/herdr/fetcher.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/stage-status.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the STAGES alignment task (the canonical list is the validation source).

## Deliverables

- Fail-soft `fetchItemsByStage` plus regression coverage.
data.title: Guard fetchItemsByStage against invalid stages

# Re-base Herdr in-progress UI behaviour on status

## Goal

As a Herdr user, I want an item being actively worked (its `status` is
`in-progress`) to keep the stage tag and the metadata Last-command panel even
though its `stage` is `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The list-row stage-tag suppression currently keyed off `item.stage === 'in_progress'` is re-based on `status === 'in-progress'` (`worklist.ts` ~1355).
- [ ] The metadata-panel Last-command reservation (`reserveLastCommand`) is re-based on `status === 'in-progress'` (`worklist.ts` ~2020-2026).
- [ ] The Last-command lookup for the metadata panel is re-based on `status === 'in-progress'` (`worklist.ts` ~6252).
- [ ] Actively-worked items (`status = 'in-progress'`, stage `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`) keep the same UI behaviour previously provided by the removed `in_progress` stage.
- [ ] Tests cover the status-based in-progress UI behaviour (list-row stage tag and Last-command panel reservation/lookup).

## Minimal Implementation

- Replace the three `stage === 'in_progress'` checks with `status === 'in-progress'` checks.
- Add/adjust tests in `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts` using `status: 'in-progress'` fixtures.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
- `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the STAGES alignment task (Stage type no longer includes `in_progress`).

## Deliverables

- Status-based in-progress UI behaviour with tests.
data.title: Re-base Herdr in-progress UI behaviour on status

# Align remaining Herdr stage consumers (grouping/hydrator)

## Goal

As a Herdr maintainer, I want the remaining Herdr modules (grouping and
hydrator) to stop treating `in_progress` as a valid stage, so no Herdr code
hard-codes a stage value the `wl` CLI rejects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` no longer references `in_progress` as a stage: the Group N filter, the "Other" filter and `WITHIN_GROUP_STAGE_ORDER` are updated, with "actively worked first" ordering derived from `status === 'in-progress'`.
- [ ] `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` `ALLOWED_STAGES_BY_STATUS` no longer lists `in_progress` for the `open` and `in-progress` statuses, matching `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml` status/stage compatibility.
- [ ] Tests cover the re-based grouping/ordering and hydrator stage compatibility.
- [ ] A repo-wide grep confirms no Herdr source hard-codes `in_progress`/`completed` as a valid stage.

## Minimal Implementation

- Update the grouping group-assignment filters and within-group stage order; base the "active first" ordering on status.
- Trim the `ALLOWED_STAGES_BY_STATUS` lists in the hydrator.
- Update `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` fixtures and expectations.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the STAGES alignment task (aligned vocabulary is the reference).

## Deliverables

- Grouping and hydrator aligned to the CLI stage vocabulary, with tests.
data.title: Align remaining Herdr stage consumers (grouping/hydrator)

# Verify done and unknown stage icon rendering

## Goal

As a Herdr user, I want legacy items carrying `stage=done` to render the
completed-style checkmark, and unknown stages to fall back deterministically
rather than show a misleading icon.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` `STAGE_ICONS`, `STAGE_FALLBACK` and `stageColor` include `done` mapped to the completed-style checkmark/colour.
- [ ] Every valid stage (including `done`) renders deterministically.
- [ ] An unknown stage falls back to the question-mark icon (and default colour) without throwing.
- [ ] New/updated tests cover `done` and an unknown stage.
- [ ] Legacy `stage=in_progress` rows (one persisted row today) continue to render fail-soft without throwing.

## Minimal Implementation

- Confirm/retain the `done` keys in the shared icon/colour maps.
- Keep legacy rendering fail-soft; remove the now-invalid `in_progress`/`completed` entries only if legacy rendering remains deterministic.
- Extend `packages/herdr/src/icons.test.ts` with `done` and unknown-stage cases.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the STAGES alignment task (icon vocabulary follows the stage vocabulary).

## Deliverables

- Verified deterministic `done` and unknown-stage icon/colour rendering with tests.
data.title: Verify done and unknown stage icon rendering

# Document the aligned Herdr stage vocabulary

## Goal

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`, and any relevant `CLI.md` / docs entries describing the Herdr stage vocabulary and filter chords. (CHANGELOG.md is excluded — managed by the ship release pipeline.)
- [ ] `packages/herdr/README.md` documents the five-stage vocabulary and the filter chords / `/wl <stage>` aliases.
- [ ] The removal of the `/wl progress` alias (and any `completed` alias) is documented, including the fail-soft behaviour.
- [ ] Any relevant `CLI.md` entries describing the Herdr stage vocabulary or filter chords are updated.
- [ ] Code comments referencing the removed stages as valid are updated. (`CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship release pipeline.)

## Minimal Implementation

- Update README and CLI docs, including the stage-grouping list and `/wl <stage>` alias list (README lines ~28, ~115).
- Update inline comments in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` that enumerate the seven-stage list.

# Prevent tests posting a real Discord release notification (Release v9.9.9)

## Problem statement

Running the release test harness posts a real notification to the configured
Discord webhook, titled `Release v9.9.9`. The side effect is harmless (no data
loss, no production impact) but noisy: the message lands in a real release
channel on every test run, and tests must never perform real outbound
notifications.

## Users

- **Developer / operator running the full test suite** — should not see
  unexpected Discord noise when testing.
  - *As a developer, when I run the release tests, no message should be posted
    to the real Discord release channel.*
- **CI operator** — test runs must be deterministic and side-effect free.
  - *As a CI operator, a test run must not depend on, or mutate, any external
    service.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No real notification.** Running the identified release test harness
   produces **no outbound HTTP request to any real Discord webhook**. Verified
   by a test that fails if the real webhook would be resolved/called during the
   harness (or by asserting the notifier is stubbed and the global-config
   fallback is unreachable in the harness).
2. **Coverage retained.** The Step 8.5 notification wiring keeps test coverage
   through a mocked/stubbed notifier (the existing
   `test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs` pattern), so silencing the real send
   does not drop coverage.
3. **Regression guard.** The release integration harness cannot accidentally
   reach the real `discord-notify.js`/global webhook again — the harness injects
   a stub notifier (or an isolated global-config path/HOME), and a test pins
   this so a future copy of the real module cannot re-introduce the side effect.
4. **Testing/validation.** At least one test asserts the "no real Discord
   request" property described in AC1; the full project test suite is exercised
   locally to confirm no external notification is emitted.
5. **Docs updated.** The test-isolation rule ("tests never perform real release
   notifications") is documented in the relevant test/README or ship-skill
   reference; all related documentation, code comments, README, and any
   relevant wiki/docs-site entries are updated.
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Production behaviour unchanged.** Real releases must still post the Discord
  notification; only test runs must be silenced.
- **Fix at the harness boundary.** Prefer stubbing the notifier module or
  isolating the global config inside the test harness, consistent with the
  existing `test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs` pattern, over changing
  production notification logic.
- **No secrets, no global mutation.** Do not commit any webhook token and do
  not mutate the operator's real `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`; isolate per test
  process if the config path is redirected.
- **Minimal, targeted change.** Do not remove or weaken unrelated release tests.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` resolves the webhook via
  `resolveDiscordWebhookUrl()` in three layers: project
  `.worklog/config.private.yaml` → project `.worklog/config.yaml` → global
  `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`. The first hit wins; if none is set the
  notification is skipped.
- `run-release.js` calls `sendReleaseNotification({ version, prUrl, projectRoot })`
  at Step 8.5. The version comes from `git describe --tags --abbrev=0`.
- The offender is `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs` (shared ship
  skill test suite): it copies the **real** `discord-notify.js` into a temp
  skill layout and runs the **real** `run-release.js` with mocked `git`/`wl`/`gh`
  binaries. The mocked `git describe` returns `v9.9.9`, and the temp project
  root has no `.worklog/` config — so webhook resolution falls back to the
  operator's global `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` and a real embed titled
  `Release v9.9.9` is POSTed. The process env (including `HOME`) is inherited,
  which is why the global fallback is reachable.
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs` already replaces
  `discord-notify.js` with a recording stub and therefore does **not** send —
  this is the pattern to reuse.
- The ship skill's own `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` injects
  `fetchFn` for every `sendReleaseNotification` call, so it does not send.

## Desired change

1. In the release integration harness, inject a stub `discord-notify.js` (as
   the existing wiring test does) **or** point the harness at an isolated
   global-config path / `HOME` so no real webhook resolves.
2. Add a regression-guard assertion that the harness cannot reach the real
   notifier / global webhook (AC3).
3. Keep (or add) coverage that Step 8.5 is invoked with the resolved
   `projectRoot`, version, and PR URL.
4. Document the "tests never post real release notifications" rule.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs` — The offender: copies the real
  `discord-notify.js` and inherits `HOME`; needs a stubbed notifier (or an
  isolated global-config path) so Step 8.5 cannot send.
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs` — Reference pattern: already
  substitutes a mock notifier that records arguments; reuse this harness shape.
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — Optional test-only guard (e.g. a
  `DISABLE_DISCORD_NOTIFY`/test-env short-circuit) **only** if harness-level
  stubbing is insufficient; production behaviour must be unchanged.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` — Confirm coverage of
  `sendReleaseNotification` remains intact after the change.
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and/or the test suite README —
  Document the test-isolation rule.

## Related work

- **WL-0MN1X7DIT0UVXTC8** — Remove TUI browser-opening test (completed). Same
  class of defect: a test performing a real external side effect. Its approach
  (mock the boundary or add a test-only guard; do not change production
  behaviour) is the precedent to follow.
- **WL-0MUWEPN6X0044R43** — Consume the project CTA in release reports (open).
  Also touches the ship-skill Discord release notification composition.
- **WL-0MURIXAHY0031JIJ** — Send standup reports to discord using the same
  webhook as the ship skill (open). Shares the same webhook/config resolution;
  any test-isolation convention should be consistent across these items.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (target location).** The offending tests live in the shared ship
  skill test harness — currently provided by the agent-framework skill tree
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills/ship`, symlinked from the SorraAgents repo), not in this
  repository's own vitest suite. This repository does not currently contain a
  `skill/ship` tree. If the operator intends the fix to land in this repository
  instead, the harness must first be vendored here (separate work).
- **Risk (scope creep).** "Fixing" this by changing production
  `discord-notify.js` could weaken real release notifications. **Mitigation:**
  prefer harness-level stubbing; add a production guard only if strictly
  necessary, and keep it opt-in.
- **Risk (false safety).** Over-mocking could hide a real Step 8.5 wiring
  regression. **Mitigation:** retain the dedicated wiring test
  (`test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs`).
- **Risk (environment coupling).** Redirecting `HOME` could affect unrelated
  behaviour of the spawned `run-release.js`/`git`/`wl` mocks. **Mitigation:**
  inject an explicit `globalConfigPath` (or stub the notifier) rather than
  changing `HOME` wholesale.
- **Failure mode.** If the harness stubs the notifier but the assertion set is
  incomplete, a future test could re-copy the real module. **Mitigation:** AC3
  regression guard.
- **Scope control.** Wiring the resolved CTA into the notification is the
  separate open item WL-0MUWEPN6X0044R43 and is **not** in scope here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: **Which repository/test suite is the target of this fix?** The seed says
  "tests for ContextHub", but this repository's vitest suite does not send any
  Discord message; the only confirmed sender is the shared ship-skill
  integration test `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs`, which copies
  the real `discord-notify.js` and executes `run-release.js` with an inherited
  `HOME`, falling back to the global `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` webhook.
  Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — recorded for producer confirmation.
  **Recommended:** fix the shared ship-skill test harness in place (stub the
  notifier / isolate the global config) — that is where the side effect
  originates.
  Source: repository investigation (this intake session).
- Q: **Is the noisy message acceptable to leave until a later release, or must
  it be silenced now?** Answer (operator, seed intent): "This is harmless but
  noisy, remove it." — remove now. Source: interactive seed context.
data.title: Prevent tests posting a real Discord release notification (Release v9.9.9)
